column47:
Become an Elementary Education teacher for grades 1-6 in a fully accredited program. Prepare for a promising career in teaching in just 15 months! The Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) in Elementary Education program at Northeastern University’s College of Professional Studies prepares students to become licensed teachers of elementary education in Massachusetts, grades 1–6. The program is designed for current teachers, career changers, and recent college graduates who hold a bachelor’s degree but did not major in education, and who wish to obtain an initial teaching license. Our cohort-based MAT program is offered through a hybrid model, allowing students to learn both online and in person. Students attend synchronous classes one evening per week during the 15-month program. They also complete a full-time, yearlong internship (fall and spring semesters) in an elementary classroom, giving them practical experience from the start of their program.
Graduates of the Master of Arts in Teaching in Elementary Education program will be able to:
*   Understand and apply foundational knowledge about student development and learning differences to plan and implement effective instruction, assessment, and differentiation for students in grades 1–6.
*   Understand and apply foundational knowledge about social-emotional development and learning to create a safe, healthy, and supportive learning environment for all students in grades 1–6.
*   Understand and apply foundational knowledge about curriculum development, instructional design, and pedagogical practices to plan and implement engaging and effective instruction for students in grades 1–6.
*   Understand and apply foundational knowledge about assessment practices to monitor student learning, provide meaningful feedback, and make instructional adjustments for students in grades 1–6.
*   Understand and apply foundational knowledge about professional ethics, responsibilities, and reflective practices to engage in continuous professional growth and advocate for students and families in grades 1–6.

Students will also gain essential leadership and management skills, including the ability to communicate effectively, to lead diverse teams, to analyze complex data, and to make informed decisions that promote equity, inclusion, and student success. Graduates of the program will be prepared to work in a variety of settings within higher education, including academic affairs, student affairs, admissions, financial aid, institutional advancement, and policy development. The program emphasizes an experiential, problem-based approach to learning, allowing students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges faced by colleges and universities. column38: College of Social Sciences and Humanities
column47: The PhD in History program at Northeastern University offers rigorous, individualized training for students interested in pursuing academic careers, digital humanities, public history, and other professions that demand advanced historical research and analysis. Students tailor their work around their own research interests, in consultation with faculty in their areas of specialization. The program cultivates historians whose research and teaching are at the cutting edge of the discipline. Graduates of the program are prepared to contribute to current conversations across the academy and to engage publics beyond it. PhD students in History typically complete coursework in their first three years and dedicate themselves to research and writing for the remaining two years. The program consists of 60 semester hours of credit, including 10 courses beyond the master’s degree, plus teaching and independent research. Coursework includes a range of seminars, methods courses, and directed studies. After successfully completing comprehensive exams, students propose and then write a dissertation. All PhD students are expected to teach for at least four semesters as part of their training, typically as a teaching assistant for an introductory survey course or a research methods course. They are also expected to participate in the department’s many ongoing research and professional development workshops.

The IE PhD Program Goals are: To provide students with a solid foundation in industrial engineering and related fields through advanced coursework. To equip students with the skills to conduct original and significant research that advances the state-of-the-art in industrial engineering. To prepare students for careers in academia, industry, and government, where they can contribute to the development and application of industrial engineering principles.

column2: PhD in Marine and Environmental Sciences
column16: We seek talented and highly motivated candidates with a strong academic background, particularly in the sciences, and research interests that align with those of our faculty. Strong applicants for this PhD program will demonstrate a record of prior research experience, such as undergraduate research, field or laboratory internships, or work as a research assistant. A master's degree in marine or environmental sciences is not required. Applicants are encouraged to identify a prospective research advisor among our faculty and indicate that faculty member in their application. All applicants are required to submit an online application and the following supporting documents: Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Resume, Official Transcripts, English Language Proficiency (for international applicants), and Application Fee.
column46: Marine Biology, Environmental Science and Policy
column47: Northeastern’s Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Marine and Environmental Sciences is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for research and teaching careers in academia, government, and industry. Our faculty’s expertise spans a range of fields, including: marine biology, ecology, oceanography, environmental science, conservation, environmental policy, and environmental health. Our researchers work locally and globally to understand and address pressing challenges, such as: climate change impacts on coastal ecosystems, sustainable fisheries management, conservation of endangered species, coastal ecosystem restoration, pollution in the marine environment, and the human health effects of environmental contaminants.

column38: College of Social Sciences and Humanities and Khoury College of Computer Sciences
column47: Network Science is a rapidly growing interdisciplinary field that offers a comprehensive framework to study complex systems from a systems-level perspective. The field brings together elements from computer science, physics, sociology, and biology to analyze and model the structure and dynamics of interconnected systems. From social networks to biological networks and the internet, understanding these complex systems is crucial for addressing contemporary challenges across diverse domains, including technology, health, and society. The PhD in Network Science at Northeastern University provides students with a multidisciplinary education at the forefront of this emerging field. Our program is designed to equip students with the theoretical foundations, computational skills, and interdisciplinary perspective necessary to conduct cutting-edge research and become leaders in academia, industry, and government. Through rigorous coursework, hands-on research opportunities, and collaborations with world-renowned faculty, students will develop a deep understanding of network theory, data analysis techniques, and computational modeling. Graduates will be prepared to tackle complex real-world problems, contribute to theoretical advancements, and drive innovation in various fields where interconnected systems play a critical role.

column2: PhD in Personal Health Informatics
column16: Online application, Application fee, Official college transcripts, Statement of purpose, Two letters of recommendation, Upload a professional resumé or CV, GRE General Test (Strong applicants for the PhD in Personal Health Informatics generally have strong GRE General Test scores, with particular strength in the analytical and quantitative sections), English proficiency (for international students), Financial documentation (for international students).
column47: The PhD in Personal Health Informatics prepares students to conduct independent, interdisciplinary research at the intersection of health sciences, social sciences, and information sciences. Students develop a strong foundation in personal health informatics, including data acquisition, processing, analytics, and applications. They engage in cutting-edge research in a variety of areas, such as designing and evaluating mobile health interventions, developing intelligent systems for health behavior change, and analyzing large-scale health data for personalized recommendations. The program emphasizes a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical skills, preparing graduates for leadership roles in academia, research institutions, and industry.

column16: Admission to the PhD in Chemistry program is based on the quality of a student’s academic record, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and GRE scores (general test). International students whose native language is not English are also required to submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. A master’s degree is not a prerequisite for admission to the PhD program. However, a master’s degree may be earned en route to the PhD.
column47: The Doctor of Philosophy in Chemistry program at Northeastern University offers advanced study and research in various areas of chemistry. Students engage in rigorous coursework and cutting-edge research under the guidance of faculty mentors, leading to the completion of a dissertation. The program prepares graduates for careers in academia, industry, and government, with a strong foundation in chemical principles and experimental techniques. Areas of research include, but are not limited to, analytical, biological, inorganic, organic, physical, and theoretical chemistry, as well as chemical biology and materials chemistry. Students are expected to develop strong critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills throughout their studies.

The PhD program prepares graduates for careers in academia, industry, and government research.

column47: As one of the fastest growing fields in the country, Computer Engineering prepares students for careers in the high-tech industry as well as research and development. The program emphasizes a balance between hardware and software, and theory and practice, encompassing subjects such as VLSI, embedded systems, computer architecture, computer networks, distributed systems, information assurance, bioinformatics, and machine learning.

column2: PhD in Counseling Psychology
column16: Online Application: Complete the Northeastern University online application, selecting the College of Health Sciences as your college, and the Counseling Psychology PhD as your program. Resume/Curriculum Vitae: Submit an up-to-date resume or CV that highlights your academic and professional experiences. Statement of Purpose: Submit an essay (1,000 words maximum) describing your academic background, any research, volunteer, or work experiences related to the program, and your academic and professional goals. Be sure to outline your reasons for wanting to pursue doctoral training in Counseling Psychology and why Northeastern’s program is a good fit for you. Letters of Recommendation: Submit three letters of recommendation. Letters should be from individuals who can speak to your academic and professional abilities, especially your potential for success in a doctoral program. At least two letters should be from academic faculty members. Academic Transcripts: Provide unofficial transcripts from all colleges and universities you have attended. Official transcripts will be required upon admission. Graduate Record Examination (GRE): The GRE General Test is optional. If you choose to submit scores, they must be from an exam taken within the last five years. Northeastern University’s institutional code is 3667. English Language Proficiency: Applicants whose native language is not English are required to submit proof of English proficiency. This can be demonstrated by one of the following: A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in the United States or a country where English is the official language. Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) scores. Minimum score requirements are 100 (Internet-based) or 600 (paper-based). International English Language Testing System (IELTS) scores. Minimum score requirement is 7.5. PTE Academic (Pearson Test of English Academic) scores. Minimum score requirement is 68. Writing Sample: A writing sample is required. This can be a research paper, a thesis chapter, or a published article.
column47: With a focus on social justice and health equity, the PhD in Counseling Psychology program at Northeastern University’s Bouvé College of Health Sciences trains graduate students to become counseling psychologists who are highly skilled in clinical practice, research, advocacy, and teaching. Our program, located in Boston, Massachusetts, prepares graduates for a variety of roles within academia and healthcare settings. The PhD in Counseling Psychology program is a full-time, in-person doctoral program that includes a minimum of four years of academic coursework, clinical practicum, research, and a 1-year full-time internship. Students typically take five to six years to complete the program. Graduates of our program are eligible for licensure as psychologists in most states and are well-prepared for careers in university teaching, research, and administration; community mental health centers; medical centers; private practice; and other health service psychology settings. Upon completion of this program, you’ll be prepared to: Provide multiculturally competent and evidence-based clinical services, including assessment, diagnosis, and intervention; Conduct scholarly research in areas aligned with the program’s social justice and health equity focus, including publishing in peer-reviewed journals and presenting at professional conferences; Advocate for marginalized communities and promote systemic change through social justice initiatives; Teach and supervise future generations of counseling psychologists; Engage in lifelong learning and professional development.
column50: The PhD in Counseling Psychology program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of the American Psychological Association (APA).

column2: PhD in Criminology and Justice Policy
column16: To be eligible for admission to the PhD in Criminology and Justice Policy program, applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Strong applicants typically hold a master’s degree in criminology, criminal justice, or a related social science field, though this is not a strict requirement. Upload the following documents to your application: Current resume or curriculum vitae; A statement of purpose outlining your academic and professional goals, how a PhD in Criminology and Justice Policy will help you achieve them, and how your prior academic and professional experiences have prepared you for doctoral study. Please indicate any faculty members in the School of Criminology and Criminal Justice with whom you would like to work and why; Official transcripts from all institutions attended; Three letters of recommendation; A writing sample; Test scores (optional).
column38: College of Social Sciences and Humanities
column47: The PhD program in Criminology and Justice Policy offers students the opportunity to learn from leading scholars who are committed to both rigorous academic research and policy-relevant scholarship. The program’s unique approach emphasizes the interdisciplinary nature of criminology and justice studies, and its strong connection to urban issues, human behavior, and the processes of social and institutional change. This research-intensive program provides students with the methodological, analytical, and theoretical skills to develop independent, impactful scholarship in the field. Students will acquire the analytical and methodological expertise necessary to engage in high-impact scholarship on crime and justice, and will develop their skills as researchers and teachers to ultimately become future leaders in the field, whether in academia, government, or policy-related positions.
column99: Full tuition ($29,916/semester) plus competitive living stipend and health insurance

column2: PhD in Cybersecurity

column47: The PhD in Pharmaceutics and Drug Delivery program aims to provide students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of pharmaceutics and drug delivery, as well as the opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research in these areas. The program prepares graduates for careers in academia, the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, and government. Students will gain expertise in various aspects of drug development, including drug formulation, pharmacokinetics, biopharmaceutics, and drug delivery systems. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, enabling students to design, execute, and interpret experiments related to drug discovery and development. Graduates will be equipped to address complex challenges in drug delivery and contribute to the advancement of pharmaceutical sciences.

column47: The PhD in Pharmacology program at Northeastern University’s Bouvé College of Health Sciences offers a strong foundation in contemporary biomedical sciences. Our faculty conducts cutting-edge research in drug discovery and development, cancer biology, neuropharmacology, molecular and biochemical pharmacology, cardiovascular pharmacology, and immunology. Students in our program gain expertise in a broad range of scientific areas and acquire knowledge and skills to lead a successful career in academia, pharmaceutical industries, or government agencies. Students learn how to design and conduct hypothesis-driven research, critically evaluate scientific literature, and effectively communicate their research findings to a diverse audience.

column47: Northeastern’s PhD in Physics program emphasizes experimental, theoretical, and computational research across a broad spectrum of physics. Students explore the core topics of classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, and statistical mechanics. With faculty committed to both outstanding instruction and cutting-edge research, doctoral students are prepared to conduct independent research, write and defend a thesis, and become leaders in their fields. Students also have access to state-of-the-art facilities and equipment, including a particle accelerator, high-performance computing clusters, and a materials characterization lab.

column2: PhD in Political Science
column16:

column38: College of Social Sciences and Humanities
column47: Northeastern’s PhD in Political Science offers an innovative, rigorous, interdisciplinary approach to the study of politics and public policy. Our program leverages the university’s strengths in urban and public policy, global studies, security studies, law, and data science, with a distinctive focus on preparing students for careers as both academics and policy-oriented researchers. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in theory and methods while also allowing them to tailor their research to specific interests. Our faculty members work at the frontiers of their fields, producing cutting-edge research and engaging in public discourse. With this foundation, students pursue a rigorous course of study to become experts in their fields, contribute to scholarly and public debates, and conduct independent research.

column2: PhD in Population Health
column16: Qualifications: Candidates should hold an MS/MPH in environmental health, epidemiology, data science, environmental science, toxicology, or a related field; or a BS in a related field with strong quantitative experience and research interest in environmental health. Highly motivated students with strong critical thinking, writing, and communication skills are particularly encouraged to apply. Knowledge of a statistical software (e.g., R, SAS, STATA) is desired.

column2: PhD in Psychology
column16: Candidates for the PhD program in psychology must hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. All application materials, except official transcripts, must be submitted electronically. Applications for the PhD program are due December 1 for fall admission. All applicants are required to submit the following: Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores. Official transcripts of all undergraduate and graduate work Three letters of recommendation A statement of purpose A curriculum vitae (CV) A writing sample Applicants whose native language is not English must demonstrate English proficiency unless they have received a bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited institution where English is the primary language of instruction. Refer to the Office of Global Services website for more information regarding English proficiency requirements.
column47: Northeastern University offers a PhD in Psychology, with research training in five focus areas: behavioral neuroscience, clinical psychology, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, or social psychology. The PhD program offers a broad-based education in psychological science and prepares students for research and teaching positions in academia and for research and applied positions in industry and government. Doctoral students conduct research in collaboration with faculty in one of five focus areas: behavioral neuroscience, clinical psychology, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, or social psychology. The department has a commitment to an inclusive academic environment and welcomes a diverse community of scholars to its PhD program. For students in the clinical psychology program, successful completion of the PhD degree is a prerequisite for entry into the clinical internship. The clinical psychology program is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA). Upon completion of the PhD program in Psychology, students will be able to: Demonstrate knowledge of the current scientific literature in their chosen areas of specialization as well as the broader field of psychology. Formulate testable hypotheses and research questions and design appropriate studies to address them. Collect, analyze, and interpret data using appropriate statistical and methodological techniques. Communicate research findings effectively in both oral and written formats to scientific and general audiences. Adhere to ethical principles in the conduct of psychological research and professional practice. Apply psychological theories and research findings to real-world problems and contribute to the advancement of psychological science.
column50: The clinical psychology program is accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA).

column47: The Experiential AI Leadership graduate certificate, formerly called the Experiential PhD Leadership graduate certificate, is designed for current PhD students at Northeastern University and early career researchers in academia and industry to explore foundational concepts in data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, and how to apply these concepts in an interdisciplinary context with an emphasis on ethics, privacy, and trustworthy AI. The curriculum covers both theoretical understanding and practical applications of AI tools, culminating in an experiential project to provide a hands-on opportunity to apply the learned knowledge. The Experiential AI Leadership graduate certificate helps students and researchers develop leadership skills in guiding interdisciplinary teams and ethical, impactful research in an increasingly data-driven world. The certificate is offered by the College of Computer and Information Science and aligns with the goals of Northeastern’s Experiential PhD program. It is also suitable for students outside the Experiential PhD program who are interested in developing expertise and leadership in AI and data science.

column47: The graduate certificate in Global Doctoral Research prepares doctoral students from any discipline to engage with global dimensions of their research. Recognizing the increasing prevalence of global research in all fields, this certificate provides students with theoretical, methodological, and ethical frameworks that are necessary to conduct impactful, responsible, and ethical global research. The certificate also supports students in developing a broad range of transferable professional skills including cross-cultural communication, intercultural competencies, navigating international research collaborations, and project management. The curriculum is designed to support PhD students across all disciplines to develop these skills through experiential learning opportunities. The certificate is offered by the Graduate School of Education within the College of Professional Studies, and delivered in a hybrid format, with both online and in-person offerings.

column47: The Graduate Certificate in Postsecondary Teaching is a 15-semester-hour program for those who want to teach in postsecondary education settings such as community colleges, four-year colleges, and universities. The program is ideal for individuals with a master’s degree or higher in a content area who are interested in developing pedagogical skills. The curriculum includes courses related to understanding postsecondary learners, designing instruction, developing curriculum, assessing learning, and exploring teaching as a profession. This certificate is also appropriate for faculty currently teaching in higher education who wish to enhance their teaching effectiveness.

column2: Certificate in 3-D Animation

column38: College of Arts, Media and Design
column47: The 3D Animation graduate certificate program provides students with the fundamental knowledge and techniques to effectively use 3D modeling and animation software, such as Autodesk Maya, and gain professional experience within the expanding field of animation. You’ll learn how to develop a strong artistic foundation in traditional and current 3D production techniques. This includes modeling, lighting, texturing, rigging, rendering, and compositing, as well as character animation and motion capture. Throughout the program, you’ll build a professional portfolio to showcase your expertise in the animation industry.

Accelerate your accounting career with the Northeastern University D’Amore-McKim School of Business Master of Science in Accounting (MS) program. Offered through the D’Amore-McKim School of Business, this program is designed for aspiring leaders interested in a wide range of accounting and financial careers in corporations, financial services, public accounting, and non-profit organizations. It prepares graduates for managerial roles and leadership positions in the accounting field, equipping them with both specialized accounting expertise and a comprehensive business perspective. The curriculum delves into advanced accounting principles, financial reporting, auditing, taxation, and business analytics, complemented by core MBA subjects like finance, marketing, operations, and strategy. The program emphasizes experiential learning, including co-op opportunities, allowing students to apply classroom knowledge in real-world settings and build professional networks. Graduates are well-prepared for careers in public accounting, corporate finance, consulting, and other business sectors, with a strong foundation for professional certifications such as the CPA (Certified Public Accountant) exam.

column47: The Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AG-ACNP) program is designed for registered nurses who want to advance their careers and become board-certified Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioners. The program prepares students to provide advanced nursing care to patients with complex acute and chronic health conditions across the adult-gerontology lifespan. As an AG-ACNP, you will specialize in providing direct care to acutely and critically ill adults and older adults in various settings, including hospitals, intensive care units, emergency departments, specialty clinics, and long-term care facilities. You will collaborate with interprofessional healthcare teams to manage patient care, order and interpret diagnostic tests, prescribe medications, and perform procedures. The curriculum focuses on developing advanced assessment, diagnostic, and therapeutic skills, as well as a strong foundation in evidence-based practice, patient safety, and healthcare policy. Graduates of the AG-ACNP program are eligible to sit for national certification exams offered by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) or the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses (AACN). Overall, the AG-ACNP program at Northeastern University provides comprehensive education and clinical training to prepare advanced practice nurses to meet the growing demand for highly skilled healthcare providers in acute and critical care settings.

Application Requirements
All applicants to graduate programs at Northeastern University are required to submit the following:
*   A completed online application.
*   A nonrefundable application fee.
*   Unofficial transcripts from all institutions attended. Official transcripts will be required upon admission.
*   A personal statement outlining your career goals and reasons for pursuing the program.
*   Two letters of recommendation from professional or academic contacts.
*   A resume or curriculum vitae (CV) detailing your work experience, education, and any relevant achievements.
*   Proof of English proficiency (for international applicants).

Program-Specific Requirements
In addition to the general application requirements, applicants to the Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) Certificate program must meet the following criteria:
*   Completion of a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) or Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) degree from an accredited institution.
*   Current, unencumbered RN license.
*   A minimum of one year of full-time clinical experience as a registered nurse in an acute care setting within the last three years.

column47: The Certificate in AI Applications at Northeastern University is designed for professionals who want to develop practical skills in artificial intelligence and its applications across various industries. This program provides a strong foundation in AI principles and techniques, focusing on hands-on experience with real-world AI projects. Through hands-on projects, students gain real-world experience and develop skills in areas such as machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and deep learning. Students will also learn about the ethical considerations and societal impacts of AI applications, ensuring they are prepared to develop and deploy AI solutions responsibly. The curriculum covers key areas such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision. Students will learn how to design, implement, and deploy AI solutions using popular tools and frameworks. The program emphasizes ethical considerations and societal impacts of AI, ensuring graduates are well-rounded professionals capable of developing responsible AI applications.
